A resource-light RAG benchmark

Does document structure improve RAG?

AutoSTAIR compares ordinary chunk retrieval with a two-stage, index-guided pipeline on one long public report.

276report pages
395retrievable chunks
54authored sections
20diverse questions
Research inspiration

From STAIR's idea to a practical benchmark

IBM Research's STAIR paper uses a language model to predict a relevant leaf section from a full table of contents. AutoSTAIR asks a narrower question: can an existing authored index help a small RAG system today, without fine-tuning or generating a new hierarchy?

Paper

STAIR

Model-based section prediction over the SearchTome benchmark of 18 books. Its contribution is a trained retriever that reasons over document structure.

Our case study

AutoSTAIR

A controlled comparison over the World Bank's World Development Report 2024, using its published structure as metadata.

Controlled design

Same evidence. Same models. Different route.

Both pipelines use the same PDF, question set, embeddings, answer model, prompt, and top-k budget. The retrieval layout is the variable.

QuestionOne of 20 questions spanning growth, climate, competition, education, debt, technology, and social mobility.
→
Shared document store395 paragraph-aware passages derived from a 276-page public report.
→
Grounded answerGenerated only from retrieved evidence, with citations retained for review.
Flat routeSearch all passages directly. Broad recall, no structure gate.
Index-guided routeChoose one of 54 authored sections, then search inside it. Focused, but the first decision is critical.

What the numbers mean

The trade-off appeared in the failure cases.

01

Better focus at rank one

Index-guided RAG reached Hit@1 of 0.60 against 0.55 for flat retrieval and often produced tighter, easier-to-audit evidence.

02

A hard section gate can hide the answer

When the first-stage router chose the wrong section, the second stage could not recover. This caused complete misses on two cross-section questions.

03

Broad search was safer at larger k

Flat retrieval reached Hit@3 of 0.85 and Hit@5 of 0.90, compared with 0.80 at both depths for the structured route.

Conclusion
Use document structure as a strong routing signal, but keep a small global retrieval path as a fallback.
What this supportsAuthored structure can improve focus and first-result precision.
What it does not proveOne document and 20 questions cannot establish a universal winner.
Next experimentEvaluate hybrid routing over multiple document types and larger question sets.
AutoSTAIR

A transparent benchmark for understanding when document structure helps retrieval-augmented generation.
